content.value_statement: Next.js teams often mix Server and Client Components incorrectly. This skill provides reusable patterns for accessible, typed, App Router components.
actual_capabilities: Explains when to use Server Components and Client Components in Next.js App Router projects.
Provides templates for typed React components with props, state, effects, handlers, and Tailwind classes.
Shows patterns for protected routes, forms, loading states, toasts, and inline editing.
Covers accessibility practices such as ARIA labels, semantic HTML, focus states, and screen reader text.
Describes advanced patterns for drag and drop, polling, error boundaries, PWA storage, caching, and logging.
limitations: It is guidance only and does not include runnable project files.
Examples are tailored to one Next.js and Tailwind application structure.
It does not validate generated code against a live application.
Error logging examples require privacy review before production use.

use_cases.title: Create App Router Components
use_cases.description: Generate typed component plans that follow Server and Client Component boundaries.

use_cases.title: Add Interactive UI Patterns
use_cases.description: Build forms, protected routes, toasts, inline editing, and loading states with consistent structure.

use_cases.title: Review Frontend Standards
use_cases.description: Check component proposals against accessibility, TypeScript, Tailwind, and Next.js App Router expectations.

prompt_templates.title: Choose Component Type
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner planning a new page or component.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the frontend-component skill to decide whether my new Next.js component should be a Server Component or Client Component. Explain the choice.

prompt_templates.title: Draft Component Structure
prompt_templates.scenario: Developer creating a typed component skeleton.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the frontend-component skill to outline a TypeScript component structure for a reusable dashboard widget with props, loading state, and Tailwind classes.

prompt_templates.title: Improve Accessibility
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the frontend-component skill to review this interactive component plan for WCAG 2.1 AA accessibility gaps and suggest concrete improvements.

prompt_templates.title: Design Advanced Behavior
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced developer adding offline and performance behavior.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the frontend-component skill to plan an advanced task list component with drag and drop, offline sync, caching, error boundaries, and privacy-conscious logging.

output_examples.input: Plan a protected dashboard route in a Next.js App Router project.
output_examples.output: The response identifies it as a Client Component because it uses hooks and navigation. It includes loading, redirect, and authorization states.

output_examples.input: Improve a form component for sign up.
output_examples.output: The response separates form data, validation errors, API errors, and loading state. It also recommends accessible labels and clear submit feedback.

output_examples.input: Add offline support to a task list.
output_examples.output: The response proposes IndexedDB storage, sync status tracking, online recovery, and error handling. It notes privacy review for logging context.

best_practices: Start with Server Components and add client directives only for interactivity.
Keep accessibility requirements visible while designing each component.
Review generated examples against project conventions before implementation.
anti_patterns: Adding use client to every file without checking whether browser APIs are needed.
Copying examples without adapting types, imports, and route names.
Sending error context to logging endpoints without redaction.

faq.question: Does this skill create complete applications?
faq.answer: No. It provides component patterns and implementation guidance for Next.js frontend work.

faq.question: When should I use a Client Component?
faq.answer: Use one when the component needs hooks, event handlers, browser APIs, or real-time interactions.

faq.question: Does it support Tailwind CSS?
faq.answer: Yes. The examples use Tailwind utility classes and conditional class composition.

faq.question: Does it include accessibility guidance?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers ARIA labels, semantic HTML, focus indicators, keyboard support, and screen reader text.

faq.question: Can Claude, Codex, and Claude Code use it?
faq.answer: Yes. The report marks support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.

faq.question: Should I copy the examples directly?
faq.answer: No. Adapt imports, types, privacy controls, routes, and styling to your project.
